# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic

<h1 id="haproxy-data-plane-api-discovery">Discovery</h1>

## Return list of root endpoints

<a id="opIdgetAPIEndpoints"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /`

Returns a list of root endpoints.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "description": "string",
    "title": "string",
    "url": "string"
  }
]
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="return-list-of-root-endpoints-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[endpoints](#schemaendpoints)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Add a new AWS region

<a id="opIdcreateAWSRegion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/service_discovery/aws \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "access_key_id": "****************L7GT",
    "allowlist": [
      {
        "key": "tag-key",
        "value": "Instance:Having:This:Tag"
      }
    ],
    "denylist": [
      {
        "key": "tag:Environment",
        "value": "development"
      }
    ],
    "enabled": true,
    "id": "0",
    "ipv4_address": "private",
    "name": "frontend-service",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "retry_timeout": 1,
    "secret_access_key": "****************soLl"
  }'
```

`POST /service_discovery/aws`

Add a new AWS region.
Credentials are not required in case Dataplane API is running in an EC2 instance with proper IAM role attached.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_key_id": "****************L7GT",
  "allowlist": [
    {
      "key": "tag-key",
      "value": "Instance:Having:This:Tag"
    }
  ],
  "denylist": [
    {
      "key": "tag:Environment",
      "value": "development"
    }
  ],
  "enabled": true,
  "id": "0",
  "ipv4_address": "private",
  "name": "frontend-service",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "retry_timeout": 1,
  "secret_access_key": "****************soLl"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-new-aws-region-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[awsRegion](#schemaawsregion)|true|none|
|» access_key_id|body|string|false|AWS Access Key ID.|
|» allowlist|body|[[awsFilters](#schemaawsfilters)]|false|Specify the AWS filters used to filter the EC2 instances to add|
|» denylist|body|[[awsFilters](#schemaawsfilters)]|false|Specify the AWS filters used to filter the EC2 instances to ignore|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|none|
|» ipv4_address|body|string|true|Select which IPv4 address the Service Discovery has to use for the backend server entry|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» region|body|string|true|none|
|» retry_timeout|body|integer|true|Duration in seconds in-between data pulling requests to the AWS region|
|» secret_access_key|body|string|false|AWS Secret Access Key.|
|» server_slots_base|body|integer|false|none|
|» server_slots_growth_increment|body|integer|false|none|
|» server_slots_growth_type|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» ipv4_address|private|
|» ipv4_address|public|
|» server_slots_growth_type|linear|
|» server_slots_growth_type|exponential|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "access_key_id": "****************L7GT",
  "allowlist": [
    {
      "key": "tag-key",
      "value": "Instance:Having:This:Tag"
    }
  ],
  "denylist": [
    {
      "key": "tag:Environment",
      "value": "development"
    }
  ],
  "enabled": true,
  "id": "0",
  "ipv4_address": "private",
  "name": "frontend-service",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "retry_timeout": 1,
  "secret_access_key": "****************soLl"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-new-aws-region-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Resource created|[awsRegion](#schemaawsregion)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|The specified resource already exists|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|409|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

Adds a new ACME provider to the configuration file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_key": "string",
  "acme_provider": "string",
  "acme_vars": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "bits": 0,

    "cli"
  ],
  "contact": "string",

  "dns_delay": 0,
  "dns_timeout": 0,

  },

  "profile": "string",
  "reuse_key": "enabled"
}
```

<h3 id="add-an-acme-provider-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|
|body|body|[acme_provider](#schemaacme_provider)|true|none|
|» account_key|body|string|false|Path where the the ACME account key is stored|
|» acme_provider|body|string|false|DNS provider for the dns-01 challenge|
|» acme_vars|body|object|false|List of variables passed to the dns-01 provider (typically API keys)|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» bits|body|integer \| null|false|Number of bits used when generating an RSA certificate. Ignored when keytype is ECDSA (curves is used instead).|
|» challenge|body|string|false|ACME challenge type.|
|» challenge_ready|body|[string]|false|How to wait for the DNS propagation: either wait for a CLI event on<br>the runtime socket (useful with dataplaneapi), or let HAProxy query<br>the DNS TXT record by itself using the default resolvers, or both,<br>or none at all.<br>|
|» contact|body|string|false|Contact email for the ACME account|
|» curves|body|string|false|Curves used with the ECDSA key type|
|» directory|body|string|true|URL to the ACME provider's directory. For example:<br>https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory<br>|
|» dns_delay|body|integer \| null|false|Delay before the first DNS resolution attempt and between retries.|
|» dns_timeout|body|integer \| null|false|Timeout before DNS propagation check fails when using 'dns' in 'challenge_ready'.|
|» eab_key_id|body|string|false|Path where the EAB key id is stored|
|» eab_mac_alg|body|string|false|MAC algorithm used for EAB signing|
|» eab_mac_key|body|string|false|Path where the EAB MAC key is stored|
|» keytype|body|string|false|Type of key to generate|
|» map|body|string|false|The map which will be used to store the ACME token (key) and thumbprint|
|» metadata|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|ACME provider's name|

|» reuse_key|body|string|false|Try to reuse the private key instead of generating a new one.|

<h3 id="add-a-backend-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Backend created|[backend](#schemabackend)|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|[backend](#schemabackend)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|The specified resource already exists|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|409|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Return a backend

<a id="opIdgetBackend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/backends/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /services/haproxy/configuration/backends/{name}`

Returns one backend configuration by its name.

<h3 id="return-a-backend-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Backend name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Backend name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|

## Delete a backend

<a id="opIddeleteBackend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/backends/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /services/haproxy/configuration/backends/{name}`

Deletes a backend from the configuration by its name.

<h3 id="delete-a-backend-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Backend name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-backend-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|None|
|204|No Content|Backend deleted|None|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

|» trace_name|body|string|false|none|

|» trace_rnd_parsing|body|boolean|false|none|

## Add a new HTTP After Response Rule

<a id="opIdcreateHTTPAfterResponseRuleFrontend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/frontends/string/http_after_response_rules/0 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \

    "cond": "unless",
    "cond_test": "{ src 192.168.0.0/16 }",

    "hdr_name": "Strict-Transport-Security",
    "type": "set-header"
  }'
```

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /services/haproxy/configuration/backends/{parent_name}/http_request_rules/{index}`

|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

## Replace a server template

<a id="opIdreplaceServerTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/backends/string/server_templates/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "fqdn": "google.com",
    "num_or_range": "1-3",
    "port": 80,
    "prefix": "srv"
  }'
```

<h1 id="haproxy-data-plane-api-server">Server</h1>

## Return an array of servers

<a id="opIdgetAllServerBackend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/backends/string/servers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /services/haproxy/configuration/backends/{parent_name}/servers`

Returns all servers that are configured in specified Backend.

<h3 id="return-an-array-of-servers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|parent_name|path|string|true|Parent name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "address": "10.1.1.1",
    "name": "www",
    "port": 8080
  }
]
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="return-an-array-of-servers-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|[servers](#schemaservers)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Add a new server

<a id="opIdcreateServerBackend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/backends/string/servers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "10.1.1.1",
    "name": "www",
    "port": 8080
  }'
```

`POST /services/haproxy/configuration/backends/{parent_name}/servers`

Adds a new server in the specified Backend.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "10.1.1.1",
  "name": "www",
  "port": 8080
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-new-server-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Server created|[server](#schemaserver)|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|[server](#schemaserver)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|The specified resource already exists|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|409|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Return one server

<a id="opIdgetServerBackend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/backends/string/servers/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /services/haproxy/configuration/backends/{parent_name}/servers/{name}`

Returns one server configuration by its name in the specified Backend.

<h3 id="return-one-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Server name|
|parent_name|path|string|true|Parent name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "address": "10.1.1.1",
  "name": "www",
  "port": 8080
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="return-one-server-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|[server](#schemaserver)|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Replace a server

<a id="opIdreplaceServerBackend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/backends/string/servers/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "10.1.1.1",
    "name": "www",
    "port": 8080
  }'
```

`PUT /services/haproxy/configuration/backends/{parent_name}/servers/{name}`

## Delete a server

<a id="opIddeleteServerBackend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/backends/string/servers/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /services/haproxy/configuration/backends/{parent_name}/servers/{name}`

Deletes a server configuration by its name from the specified Backend.

<h3 id="delete-a-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Server name|
|parent_name|path|string|true|Parent name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-server-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|None|
|204|No Content|Server deleted|None|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/peers/string/servers \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```
```bash
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "10.1.1.1",
    "name": "www",
    "port": 8080
  }'
```

## Return one server

<a id="opIdgetServerRing"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/rings/string/servers/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /services/haproxy/configuration/rings/{parent_name}/servers/{name}`

Returns one server configuration by its name in the specified Ring.

<h3 id="return-one-server-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Server name|
|parent_name|path|string|true|Parent name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "address": "10.1.1.1",
  "name": "www",
  "port": 8080
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="return-one-server-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|[server](#schemaserver)|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Replace a server

<a id="opIdreplaceServerRing"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/rings/string/servers/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "10.1.1.1",
    "name": "www",
    "port": 8080
  }'
```

`PUT /services/haproxy/configuration/rings/{parent_name}/servers/{name}`

Replaces a server configuration by its name in the specified Ring.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "10.1.1.1",
  "name": "www",
  "port": 8080
}
```

|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

## Delete a server

<a id="opIddeleteServerRing"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/rings/string/servers/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /services/haproxy/configuration/rings/{parent_name}/servers/{name}`

Deletes a server configuration by its name from the specified Ring.

<h3 id="delete-a-server-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Server name|
|parent_name|path|string|true|Parent name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-server-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|None|
|204|No Content|Server deleted|None|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|crt_store|path|string|true|Parent crt_store name|

|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|

|» curves|body|string|false|Curves used with generate-dummy and the ECDSA key type (default P-384)|

<h3 id="return-an-array-of-defaults-sections-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|[defaults_sections](#schemadefaults_sections)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

<h3 id="add-a-defaults-section-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|
|body|body|[defaults](#schemadefaults)|true|none|
|» abortonclose|body|string|false|none|
|» accept_invalid_http_request|body|string|false|none|
|» accept_invalid_http_response|body|string|false|none|
|» accept_unsafe_violations_in_http_request|body|string|false|none|
|» accept_unsafe_violations_in_http_response|body|string|false|none|
|» adv_check|body|string|false|none|
|» allbackups|body|string|false|none|
|» backlog|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» balance|body|[balance](#schemabalance)|false|none|
|» check_timeout|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» checkcache|body|string|false|none|
|» clflog|body|boolean|false|none|
|» client_fin_timeout|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» client_timeout|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» clitcpka|body|string|false|none|
|» clitcpka_cnt|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» clitcpka_idle|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» clitcpka_intvl|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» compression|body|[compression](#schemacompression)|false|none|
|» connect_timeout|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» contstats|body|string|false|none|

<h3 id="add-a-defaults-section-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Defaults section created|[defaults](#schemadefaults)|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|[defaults](#schemadefaults)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|The specified resource already exists|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|409|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

<h3 id="add-a-defaults-section-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Defaults section created|[defaults](#schemadefaults)|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|[defaults](#schemadefaults)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|The specified resource already exists|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|409|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Return a defaults section

<a id="opIdgetDefaultsSection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/defaults/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /services/haproxy/configuration/defaults/{name}`

Returns one defaults section configuration by its name.

<h3 id="return-a-defaults-section-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Defaults section name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|

<h3 id="return-a-defaults-section-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|[defaults](#schemadefaults)|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Delete a defaults section

<a id="opIddeleteDefaultsSection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/defaults/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /services/haproxy/configuration/defaults/{name}`

Deletes a defaults section from the configuration by its name.

<h3 id="delete-a-defaults-section-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Defaults section name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-defaults-section-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|None|
|204|No Content|Defaults section deleted|None|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/defaults/string/quic_initial_rules \
```
```bash
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-fcgi-app-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|None|
|204|No Content|FCGI app deleted|None|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

<h1 id="haproxy-data-plane-api-frontend">Frontend</h1>

## Return an array of frontends

<a id="opIdgetFrontends"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/frontends \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /services/haproxy/configuration/frontends`

Returns an array of all configured frontends.

<h3 id="return-an-array-of-frontends-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|

`POST /services/haproxy/configuration/frontends`

Adds a new frontend to the configuration file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "default_backend": "test_backend",
```

<h3 id="add-a-frontend-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|

<h3 id="add-a-frontend-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Frontend created|[frontend](#schemafrontend)|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|[frontend](#schemafrontend)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|The specified resource already exists|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|409|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Return a frontend

<a id="opIdgetFrontend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/frontends/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /services/haproxy/configuration/frontends/{name}`

Returns one frontend configuration by its name.

<h3 id="return-a-frontend-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Frontend name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|

<h3 id="return-a-frontend-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|[frontend](#schemafrontend)|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

|name|path|string|true|Frontend name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|

## Delete a frontend

<a id="opIddeleteFrontend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/frontends/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /services/haproxy/configuration/frontends/{name}`

Deletes a frontend from the configuration by its name.

<h3 id="delete-a-frontend-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Frontend name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

## Delete a bind

<a id="opIddeleteBindFrontend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/frontends/string/binds/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /services/haproxy/configuration/frontends/{parent_name}/binds/{name}`

Deletes a bind configuration by its name from the specified Frontend.

<h3 id="delete-a-bind-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Bind name|
|parent_name|path|string|true|Parent name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-bind-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|None|
|204|No Content|Bind deleted|None|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

basic_auth

## Delete a bind

<a id="opIddeleteBindLogForward"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/log_forwards/string/binds/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /services/haproxy/configuration/log_forwards/{parent_name}/binds/{name}`

Deletes a bind configuration by its name from the specified LogForward.

<h3 id="delete-a-bind-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Bind name|
|parent_name|path|string|true|Parent name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-bind-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|None|
|204|No Content|Bind deleted|None|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

<h3 id="add-a-new-bind-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Bind created|[bind](#schemabind)|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|[bind](#schemabind)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|The specified resource already exists|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|409|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Return one bind

<a id="opIdgetBindPeer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/peers/string/binds/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /services/haproxy/configuration/peers/{parent_name}/binds/{name}`

Returns one bind configuration by its name in the specified Peer.

|parent_name|path|string|true|Parent name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|

<h3 id="replace-a-ssl-front-use-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|SSL Front Use replaced|[ssl_front_use](#schemassl_front_use)|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|[ssl_front_use](#schemassl_front_use)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Delete a SSL Front Use

<a id="opIddeleteSSLFrontUse"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/frontends/string/ssl_front_uses/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /services/haproxy/configuration/frontends/{parent_name}/ssl_front_uses/{index}`

Deletes a SSL Front Use configuration by its index from the specified Frontend.

<h3 id="delete-a-ssl-front-use-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|index|path|integer|true|SSL Front Use Index|
|parent_name|path|string|true|Parent name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-ssl-front-use-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|None|
|204|No Content|SSL Front Use deleted|None|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

<h3 id="return-an-array-of-log-forwards-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|[log_forwards](#schemalog_forwards)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

<h3 id="add-a-log-forward-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|
|body|body|[log_forward](#schemalog_forward)|true|none|
|» assume-rfc6587-ntf|body|boolean|false|none|
|» backlog|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» dont-parse-log|body|boolean|false|none|
|» maxconn|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» timeout_client|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» binds|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[bind](#schemabind)|false|HAProxy frontend bind configuration|
|» dgram_binds|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[dgram_bind](#schemadgram_bind)|false|HAProxy log forward dgram bind configuration|
|» log_target_list|body|[log_targets](#schemalog_targets)|false|HAProxy log target array (corresponds to log directives)|

<h3 id="add-a-log-forward-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Log forward created|[log_forward](#schemalog_forward)|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|[log_forward](#schemalog_forward)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|The specified resource already exists|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|409|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Return a log forward

<a id="opIdgetLogForward"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/log_forwards/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /services/haproxy/configuration/log_forwards/{name}`

Returns one log forward configuration by its name.

<h3 id="return-a-log-forward-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Log forward name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|

<a id="opIdreplaceLogForward"></a>

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "assume-rfc6587-ntf": true,
```

<h3 id="replace-a-log-forward-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Log forward name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|
|body|body|[log_forward](#schemalog_forward)|true|none|
|» assume-rfc6587-ntf|body|boolean|false|none|
|» backlog|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» dont-parse-log|body|boolean|false|none|
|» maxconn|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» timeout_client|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» binds|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[bind](#schemabind)|false|HAProxy frontend bind configuration|
|» dgram_binds|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[dgram_bind](#schemadgram_bind)|false|HAProxy log forward dgram bind configuration|
|» log_target_list|body|[log_targets](#schemalog_targets)|false|HAProxy log target array (corresponds to log directives)|

## Delete a log forward

<a id="opIddeleteLogForward"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/log_forwards/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /services/haproxy/configuration/log_forwards/{name}`

Deletes a log forward from the configuration by its name.

<h3 id="delete-a-log-forward-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Log forward name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|None|
|204|No Content|Log forward deleted|None|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="return-an-array-of-peer-sections-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|[peer_sections](#schemapeer_sections)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

<h3 id="add-a-peer-section-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|
|body|body|[peer_section](#schemapeer_section)|true|none|
|» default_bind|body|[default_bind](#schemadefault_bind)|false|HAProxy default bind configuration|
|» default_server|body|[default_server](#schemadefault_server)|false|none|
|» disabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» shards|body|integer|false|In some configurations, one would like to distribute the stick-table contents<br>to some peers in place of sending all the stick-table contents to each peer<br>declared in the "peers" section. In such cases, "shards" specifies the<br>number of peer involved in this stick-table contents distribution.|
|» binds|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[bind](#schemabind)|false|HAProxy frontend bind configuration|
|» log_target_list|body|[log_targets](#schemalog_targets)|false|HAProxy log target array (corresponds to log directives)|
|» peer_entries|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[peer_entry](#schemapeer_entry)|false|Peer Entry from peers table|
|» servers|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[server](#schemaserver)|false|HAProxy backend server configuration|
|» tables|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[table](#schematable)|false|none|

<h3 id="add-a-peer-section-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Peer section created|[peer_section](#schemapeer_section)|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|[peer_section](#schemapeer_section)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|The specified resource already exists|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Reload-ID|string||ID of the requested reload|
|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|409|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|default|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## Return a peer section

<a id="opIdgetPeerSection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/configuration/peer_section/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /services/haproxy/configuration/peer_section/{name}`

Returns one peer section configuration by its name.

<h3 id="return-a-peer-section-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Peer section name|
|transaction_id|query|string|false|ID of the transaction where we want to add the operation. Cannot be used when version is specified.|
|full_section|query|boolean|false|Indicates if the action affects the specified child resources as well|

`POST /services/haproxy/configuration/raw`

```text
string
```

<h3 id="push-new-haproxy-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|query|integer|false|Version used for checking configuration version. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, transaction has its own version.|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|
|skip_version|query|boolean|false|If set, no version check will be done and the pushed configuration will be applied directly.|
|skip_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, HAProxy will not be reloaded after the configuration is pushed.|
|only_validate|query|boolean|false|If set, the configuration will only be validated and not applied.|
|X-Runtime-Actions|header|string|false|List of runtime actions to execute after the configuration is applied.|
|body|body|string|true|none|

## Commit transaction

<a id="opIdcommitTransaction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:5555/v3/services/haproxy/transactions/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`PUT /services/haproxy/transactions/{id}`

Commit transaction, execute all operations in transaction and return msg

<h3 id="commit-transaction-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Transaction id|
|force_reload|query|boolean|false|If set, do a force reload, do not wait for the configured reload-delay. Cannot be used when transaction is specified, as changes in transaction are not applied directly to configuration.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_version": 2,
  "id": "273e3385-2d0c-4fb1-aa27-93cbb31ff203",
  "status": "in_progress"
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "_version": 2,
  "id": "273e3385-2d0c-4fb1-aa27-93cbb31ff203",
  "status": "in_progress"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> 406 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "property1": "string",
  "property2": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="commit-transaction-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Transaction successfully committed|[transaction](#schematransaction)|
|202|Accepted|Configuration change accepted and reload requested|[transaction](#schematransaction)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|The specified resource was not found|[error](#schemaerror)|
|406|Not Acceptable|The specified resource cannot be handled|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|General Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|202|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

|400|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|404|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|
|406|Configuration-Version|string||Configuration file version|

<h2 id="tocS_acme_provider">acme_provider</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaacme_provider"></a>
<a id="schema_acme_provider"></a>
<a id="tocSacme_provider"></a>
<a id="tocsacme_provider"></a>

```json
{
  "account_key": "string",
  "acme_provider": "string",
  "acme_vars": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "bits": 0,
  "challenge": "http-01",
  "challenge_ready": [
    "cli"
  ],
  "contact": "string",
  "curves": "string",
  "directory": "string",
  "dns_delay": 0,
  "dns_timeout": 0,
  "eab_key_id": "string",
  "eab_mac_alg": "HS256",
  "eab_mac_key": "string",
  "keytype": "RSA",
  "map": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  },
  "name": "string",
  "profile": "string",
  "reuse_key": "enabled"
}
```

Define an ACME provider to generate certificates automatically

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_key|string|false|none|Path where the the ACME account key is stored|
|acme_provider|string|false|none|DNS provider for the dns-01 challenge|
|acme_vars|object|false|none|List of variables passed to the dns-01 provider (typically API keys)|
|bits|integer \| null|false|none|Number of bits used when generating an RSA certificate. Ignored when keytype is ECDSA (curves is used instead).|
|challenge|string|false|none|ACME challenge type.|
|challenge_ready|[string]|false|none|How to wait for the DNS propagation: either wait for a CLI event on<br>the runtime socket (useful with dataplaneapi), or let HAProxy query<br>the DNS TXT record by itself using the default resolvers, or both,<br>or none at all.<br>|
|contact|string|false|none|Contact email for the ACME account|
|curves|string|false|none|Curves used with the ECDSA key type|
|directory|string|true|none|URL to the ACME provider's directory. For example:<br>https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory<br>|
|dns_delay|integer \| null|false|none|Delay before the first DNS resolution attempt and between retries.|
|dns_timeout|integer \| null|false|none|Timeout before DNS propagation check fails when using 'dns' in 'challenge_ready'.|
|eab_key_id|string|false|none|Path where the EAB key id is stored|
|eab_mac_alg|string|false|none|MAC algorithm used for EAB signing|
|eab_mac_key|string|false|none|Path where the EAB MAC key is stored|
|keytype|string|false|none|Type of key to generate|
|map|string|false|none|The map which will be used to store the ACME token (key) and thumbprint|
|metadata|object|false|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|ACME provider's name|
|profile|string|false|none|Request a specific certificate profile from the CA by including a 'profile'<br>field in the newOrder request (draft-ietf-acme-profiles). Profile names<br>are CA-specific short identifiers (e.g. 'classic', 'shortlived').<br>|
|reuse_key|string|false|none|Try to reuse the private key instead of generating a new one.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|challenge|http-01|
|challenge|dns-01|
|challenge|dns-persist-01|
|challenge_ready|cli|
|challenge_ready|dns|
|challenge_ready|none|
|eab_mac_alg|HS256|
|eab_mac_alg|HS384|
|eab_mac_alg|HS512|
|keytype|RSA|
|keytype|ECDSA|
|reuse_key|enabled|
|reuse_key|disabled|

App with all its children resources

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|docroot|string|true|none|Defines the document root on the remote host. The parameter serves to build the default value of FastCGI parameters SCRIPT_FILENAME and PATH_TRANSLATED. It is a mandatory setting.|
|get_values|string|false|none|Enables or disables the retrieval of variables related to connection management.|
|index|string|false|none|Defines the script name to append after a URI that ends with a slash ("/") to set the default value for the FastCGI parameter SCRIPT_NAME. It is an optional setting.|
|keep_conn|string|false|none|Tells the FastCGI application whether or not to keep the connection open after it sends a response. If disabled, the FastCGI application closes the connection after responding to this request.|
|log_stderrs|[[fcgi_log_stderr](#schemafcgi_log_stderr)]|false|none|none|
|max_reqs|integer|false|none|Defines the maximum number of concurrent requests this application can accept. If the FastCGI application retrieves the variable FCGI_MAX_REQS during connection establishment, it can override this option. Furthermore, if the application does not do multiplexing, it will ignore this option.|
|metadata|object|false|none|none|
|mpxs_conns|string|false|none|Enables or disables the support of connection multiplexing. If the FastCGI application retrieves the variable FCGI_MPXS_CONNS during connection establishment, it can override this option.|
|name|string|true|none|Declares a FastCGI application|
|pass_headers|[[fcgi_pass_header](#schemafcgi_pass_header)]|false|none|none|
|path_info|string|false|none|Defines a regular expression to extract the script-name and the path-info from the URI.<br>Thus, <regex> must have two captures: the first to capture the script name, and the second to capture the path- info.<br>If not defined, it does not perform matching on the URI, and does not fill the FastCGI parameters PATH_INFO and PATH_TRANSLATED.|
|set_params|[[fcgi_set_param](#schemafcgi_set_param)]|false|none|none|
|acl_list|[acls](#schemaacls)|false|none|HAProxy ACL lines array (corresponds to acl directives)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|get_values|enabled|
|get_values|disabled|
|keep_conn|enabled|
|keep_conn|disabled|
|mpxs_conns|enabled|
|mpxs_conns|disabled|

<h2 id="tocS_fcgi_pass_header">fcgi_pass_header</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafcgi_pass_header"></a>
<a id="schema_fcgi_pass_header"></a>
<a id="tocSfcgi_pass_header"></a>
<a id="tocsfcgi_pass_header"></a>

```json
{
  "cond": "if",
  "cond_test": "string",
  "name": "string"
}
```

Specifies the name of a request header to pass to the FastCGI application.
Optionally, you can follow it with an ACL-based condition, in which case the FastCGI application evaluates it only if the condition is true.
Most request headers are already available to the FastCGI application with the prefix "HTTP".
Thus, you only need this directive to pass headers that are purposefully omitted.
Currently, the headers "Authorization", "Proxy-Authorization", and hop-by-hop headers are omitted.
Note that the headers "Content-type" and "Content-length" never pass to the FastCGI application because they are already converted into parameters.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cond|string|false|none|none|
|cond_test|string|false|none|none|
|name|string|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|cond|if|
|cond|unless|

HAProxy filters

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|app_name|string|false|none|Name of the fcgi-app section this filter will use.|
|bandwidth_limit_name|string|false|none|Filter name that will be used by 'set-bandwidth-limit' actions to reference a specific bandwidth limitation filter|
|cache_name|string|false|none|none|
|default_limit|integer|false|none|The max number of bytes that can be forwarded over the period.<br>The value must be specified for per-stream and shared bandwidth limitation filters.<br>It follows the HAProxy size format and is expressed in bytes.|
|default_period|integer|false|none|The default time period used to evaluate the bandwidth limitation rate.<br>It can be specified for per-stream bandwidth limitation filters only.<br>It follows the HAProxy time format and is expressed in milliseconds.|
|key|string|false|none|A sample expression rule.<br>It describes what elements will be analyzed, extracted, combined, and used to select which table entry to update the counters.<br>It must be specified for shared bandwidth limitation filters only.|
|limit|integer|false|none|The max number of bytes that can be forwarded over the period.<br>The value must be specified for per-stream and shared bandwidth limitation filters.<br>It follows the HAProxy size format and is expressed in bytes.|
|lua_args|[string]|false|none|Optional arguments passed to the Lua filter constructor.|
|lua_name|string|false|none|Name of the Lua filter as registered by core.register_filter(), used in the 'filter lua.<name>' directive.|
|metadata|object|false|none|none|
|min_size|integer|false|none|The optional minimum number of bytes forwarded at a time by a stream excluding the last packet that may be smaller.<br>This value can be specified for per-stream and shared bandwidth limitation filters.<br>It follows the HAProxy size format and is expressed in bytes.|
|spoe_config|string|false|none|none|
|spoe_engine|string|false|none|none|
|table|string|false|none|An optional table to be used instead of the default one, which is the stick-table declared in the current proxy.<br>It can be specified for shared bandwidth limitation filters only.|

<h2 id="tocS_forwarded">forwarded</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaforwarded"></a>
<a id="schema_forwarded"></a>
<a id="tocSforwarded"></a>
<a id="tocsforwarded"></a>

```json
{
  "by": true,
  "by_expr": "string",
  "by_port": true,
  "by_port_expr": "string",
  "enabled": "enabled",
  "for": true,
  "for_expr": "string",
  "for_port": true,
  "for_port_expr": "string",
  "host": true,
  "host_expr": "string",
  "proto": true
}
```

Controls insertion of the HTTP Forwarded header field.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|by|boolean|false|none|Adds the by parameter using the local address.|
|by_expr|string|false|none|Adds the by parameter using the specified log-format expression.|
|by_port|boolean|false|none|Adds the by parameter port using the local port.|
|by_port_expr|string|false|none|Adds the by parameter port using the specified log-format expression.|
|enabled|string|true|none|Enables or disables insertion of the HTTP Forwarded header field.|
|for|boolean|false|none|Adds the for parameter using the client address.|
|for_expr|string|false|none|Adds the for parameter using the specified log-format expression.|
|for_port|boolean|false|none|Adds the for parameter port using the client port.|
|for_port_expr|string|false|none|Adds the for parameter port using the specified log-format expression.|
|host|boolean|false|none|Adds the host parameter using the request authority.|
|host_expr|string|false|none|Adds the host parameter using the specified log-format expression.|
|proto|boolean|false|none|Adds the proto parameter using the incoming request protocol.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|enabled|enabled|
|enabled|disabled|

```json
  "allow_none_alg": true,
  "decrypt_alg_list": "string",
  "decrypt_enc_list": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_none_alg|boolean|false|none|Allow unsigned JWTs using the none algorithm in the jwt_verify converter.|

|decrypt_enc_list|string|false|none|Colon-separated list of allowed JWT encryption algorithms; supports ALL and exclusions prefixed with !.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|busy_polling|boolean|false|none|none|
|fd_hard_limit|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|max_spread_checks|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|maxcompcpuusage|integer|false|none|none|
|maxcomprate|integer|false|none|Maximum per-process input compression rate|
|maxconn|integer|false|none|none|
|maxconnrate|integer|false|none|Maximum per-process number of concurrent connections|
|maxpipes|integer|false|none|none|
|maxsessrate|integer|false|none|Maximum per-process number of sessions per second|
|maxzlibmem|integer|false|none|Maximum amount of RAM in megabytes per process usable by the zlib|
|no_memory_trimming|boolean|false|none|Disables memory trimming (malloc_trim) on memory shortage or reload|
|noepoll|boolean|false|none|Disable the use of the "epoll" event polling system on Linux|
|noevports|boolean|false|none|Disable the use of the event ports event polling system on SunOS system derived from Solaris 10 and later|
|nogetaddrinfo|boolean|false|none|Disable the use of getaddrinfo for name resolving|
|nokqueue|boolean|false|none|Disable the use of the "kqueue" event polling system on BSD|
|noktls|boolean|false|none|Disables the use of ktls. It is equivalent to the command line argument "-dT"|
|nopoll|boolean|false|none|Disable the use of the "poll" event polling system|
|noreuseport|boolean|false|none|none|
|nosplice|boolean|false|none|Disable the use of kernel tcp splicing between sockets on Linux|
|profiling_memory|string|false|none|Enable or disables per-function memory profiling|
|profiling_tasks|string|false|none|Enable or disables per-task CPU profiling|
|server_state_base|string|false|none|none|
|server_state_file|string|false|none|none|
|spread_checks|integer|false|none|Add some randomness in the check interval|
|thread_hard_limit|integer \| null|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

|profiling_memory|disabled|
|profiling_tasks|auto|
|profiling_tasks|enabled|

<h2 id="tocS_server_switching_rule">server_switching_rule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaserver_switching_rule"></a>
<a id="schema_server_switching_rule"></a>
<a id="tocSserver_switching_rule"></a>
<a id="tocsserver_switching_rule"></a>

```json
{
  "cond": "if",
  "cond_test": "{ req.ssl_sni -i www.example.com }",
  "target_server": "www"
}
```

HAProxy server switching rule configuration (corresponds to use-server directive)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cond|string|false|none|none|
|cond_test|string|false|none|none|
|metadata|object|false|none|none|
|target_server|string|true|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|cond|if|
|cond|unless|

<h2 id="tocS_site">site</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasite"></a>
<a id="schema_site"></a>
<a id="tocSsite"></a>
<a id="tocssite"></a>

```json
{
  "farms": [
    {
      "balance": {
        "algorithm": "roundrobin"
      },
      "mode": "http",
      "name": "www_backend",
      "servers": [
        {
          "address": "127.0.1.1",
          "name": "www_server",
          "port": 4567
        },
        {
          "address": "127.0.1.2",
          "name": "www_server_new",
          "port": 4567
        }
      ],
      "use_as": "default"
    }
  ],
  "name": "test_site",
  "service": {
    "http_connection_mode": "httpclose",
    "maxconn": 2000,
    "mode": "http"
  }
}
```

Site configuration. Sites are considered as one service and all farms connected to that service.
Farms are connected to service using use-backend and default_backend directives. Sites let you
configure simple HAProxy configurations, for more advanced options use /haproxy/configuration
endpoints.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|farms|[object]|false|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|service|object|false|none|none|
